title: Getting started
text: urbioconnect implements habitat connectivity method described Kirk et al. (2023): Kirk, H., Soanes, K., Amati, M., Bekessy, S., Harrison, L., Parris, K., Ramalho, C., van de Ree, R., & Threlfall, C. (2023). Ecological connectivity planning tool conservation wildlife cities. MethodsX, 10, 101989. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.mex.2022.101989 core idea two habitat patches considered connected animal can travel without crossing barrier (e.g., road). buffer habitat species-specific movement distance, cut buffers wherever barriers exist. remaining pieces habitat connected become patches, summarise areas compute connectivity metrics. workflow represented visually figure , paper Kirk et al.:  vignette walks raster workflow step step using built-Blue-tongued Lizard example data Darebin Creek, Melbourne. show run workflow single function call.

title: Getting started
text: package ships habitat barrier rasters Blue-tongued Lizard study area along Darebin Creek, Preston West Heidelberg, Melbourne. habitat raster value 1 lizard habitat exists, NA elsewhere.  barrier raster value 1 barriers (roads exist), 0 elsewhere.  can see overlaid:  dispersal distance blue-tongued lizard environment normally 1,000m, suggess buffer distance 500 m – half connectivity threshold. means two patches considered connected outside edges within 500 metres . 500m accurate, examples use smaller buffer distance increase computational speed.
code: habitat <- example_habitat() barrier <- example_barrier()  habitat #> class       : SpatRaster #> size        : 763, 766, 1  (nrow, ncol, nlyr) #> resolution  : 2, 2  (x, y) #> extent      : 326109.6, 327641.6, 5820362, 5821888  (xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax) #> coord. ref. : GDA94 / MGA zone 55 (EPSG:28355) #> source      : lizard_habitat_raster.tif #> name        : Pseudo Layer #> min value   :            1 #> max value   :            1 barrier #> class       : SpatRaster #> size        : 763, 766, 1  (nrow, ncol, nlyr) #> resolution  : 2, 2  (x, y) #> extent      : 326109.6, 327641.6, 5820362, 5821888  (xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax) #> coord. ref. : GDA94 / MGA zone 55 (EPSG:28355) #> source      : lizard_barrier_raster.tif #> name        : layer #> min value   :     0 #> max value   :     1 plot(habitat, main = "Lizard Habitat", col = "seagreen", legend = FALSE) plot(barrier, main = "Lizard Barriers", col = c("white", "black"), legend = FALSE) plot(barrier, main = "Lizard Habitat and Barrier", col = c("white", "black"), legend = FALSE) plot(habitat, col = "seagreen", add = TRUE, legend = FALSE)

title: Getting started
text: Let’s now break step pipeline: Create barrier mask Remove habitat barriers Buffer habitat Fragment habitat along barriers Assign patch IDs Summarise patch areas

title: Getting started
text: create_barrier_mask() converts barrier raster (1 = barrier, NA = passable) multiplier mask (NA = barrier, 1 = passable). format lets us block movement multiplying layers together.
code: barrier_mask <- create_barrier_mask(barrier) plot(barrier_mask, col = c("grey"), legend = FALSE)

title: Getting started
text: Habitat sitting directly beneath barrier removed analysis. Roads bisecting habitat patch effectively remove habitat connectivity purposes. can see habitats removed - green spaces habitat kep, orange ones habitat intersected barriers.
code: remaining_habitat <- drop_habitat_under_barrier(   habitat = habitat,   barrier_mask = barrier_mask ) plot(barrier_mask, col = c("grey"), legend = FALSE) plot(habitat, col = "#d95f02", legend = FALSE, add = TRUE) plot(remaining_habitat, col = "#1b9e77", legend = FALSE, add = TRUE)

title: Getting started
text: habitat_buffer() expands habitat outward using circular focal window. buffer distance half species’ connectivity threshold. example, two patches considered connected within 200 m , use 100 m buffer, buffers overlap patches within 200 m. blue-tongued lizard urban Melbourne, median dispersal distance 1000 m (Kirk et al., 2023), use buffer 500 m. However, use 10 faster demonstration small example dataset.  can now visualise three layers together using gg_barrier_habitat_buffer():
code: buffer_distance <- 10  buffered_habitat <- habitat_buffer(   habitat = remaining_habitat,   distance = buffer_distance )  plot(barrier_mask, col = scales::alpha("grey", 1), legend = FALSE) plot(buffered_habitat, col = "darkgreen", legend = FALSE, add = TRUE) plot(remaining_habitat, col = "#1b9e77", legend = FALSE, add = TRUE) gg_barrier_habitat_buffer(   barrier = barrier,   buffered = buffered_habitat,   habitat = remaining_habitat,   distance = buffer_distance,   species_name = "Blue-tongued Lizard",   col_barrier = "grey30",   col_buffer = "lightgreen",   col_habitat = "#1b9e77",   col_paper = "white" ) #> <SpatRaster> resampled to 500554 cells. #> <SpatRaster> resampled to 500554 cells. #> <SpatRaster> resampled to 500554 cells.

title: Getting started
text: fragment_habitat() cuts buffered habitat wherever barrier cell exists. step disconnects patches separated roads.
code: fragmented <- fragment_habitat(   buffered_habitat = buffered_habitat,   barrier_mask = barrier_mask )  fragmented #> class       : SpatRaster #> size        : 763, 766, 1  (nrow, ncol, nlyr) #> resolution  : 2, 2  (x, y) #> extent      : 326109.6, 327641.6, 5820362, 5821888  (xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax) #> coord. ref. : GDA94 / MGA zone 55 (EPSG:28355) #> source(s)   : memory #> varname     : lizard_habitat_raster #> name        : focal_max #> min value   :         1 #> max value   :         1

title: Getting started
text: assign_patches_to_fragments() labels habitat cell integer identifying connected patch belongs . Habitat cells share fragment blob get patch ID. add_patch_area() appends cell-area layer raster, needed area calculations next step. can plot patches, connected patch shown distinct colour using plot_patches():
code: patch_id_raster <- assign_patches_to_fragments(   remaining_habitat = remaining_habitat,   fragment = fragmented ) |>   add_patch_area()  patch_id_raster #> class       : SpatRaster #> size        : 763, 766, 2  (nrow, ncol, nlyr) #> resolution  : 2, 2  (x, y) #> extent      : 326109.6, 327641.6, 5820362, 5821888  (xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax) #> coord. ref. : GDA94 / MGA zone 55 (EPSG:28355) #> source(s)   : memory #> varnames    : lizard_habitat_raster #>               lizard_habitat_raster #> names       : patch_id,     area #> min values  :        1, 4.000221 #> max values  :      406, 4.000273 plot_patches(   patch_id = patch_id_raster,   distance = buffer_distance,   species_name = "Blue-tongued Lizard" ) #> <SpatRaster> resampled to 500554 cells.

title: Getting started
text: aggregate_connected_patches() collapses raster one row per patch, summing area habitat cells within patch. result three columns: patch_id - integer identifier connected patch area - total habitat area within patch (square metres) area_squared - squared area, used connectivity metrics

title: Getting started
text: summarise_connectivity() takes patch area data computes set landscape-level connectivity metrics: two key metrics : Effective mesh size (ha) - average area patch randomly chosen animal finds . Larger values mean better connectivity: meff=∑Ai2∑Ai×0.0001m_{\text{eff}} = \frac{\sum A_i^2}{\sum A_i} \times 0.0001 Probability connectedness - probability two randomly chosen points within habitat connected patch. Ranges 0 (fully fragmented) 1 (habitat connected): Pc=mefftotal habitat areaP_c = \frac{m_{\text{eff}}}{\text{total habitat area}} AiA_i area given patch.
code: results <- summarise_connectivity(   area = areas_connected$area,   buffer_distance = buffer_distance,   target_resolution = 500,   data_resolution = 10,   aggregation_factor = 50,   species_name = "Blue-tongued Lizard" )  results #> # A tibble: 1 × 10 #>   species_name    buffer_distance n_patches effective_mesh_ha prob_connectedness #>   <chr>                     <dbl>     <int>             <dbl>              <dbl> #> 1 Blue-tongued L…              10       163                 4           0.000017 #> # ℹ 5 more variables: patch_area_mean <dbl>, patch_area_total_ha <dbl>, #> #   target_resolution <dbl>, data_resolution <dbl>, aggregation_factor <dbl>

text: common workflow run analysis several buffer distances compare results. Use purrr::map() iterate, purrr::list_rbind() combine: multiple buffer distances can visualise connectivity changes using plot_connectivity():  plot_connectivity() produces faceted ggplot2 figure showing connectivity metric (number patches, probability connectedness, mean patch area, total habitat area) function buffer distance.

title: Getting started
text: core raster workflow urbioconnect : create_barrier_mask() - invert barrier raster passability mask drop_habitat_under_barrier() - remove habitat beneath barriers habitat_buffer() - expand habitat movement distance (half connectivity threshold) fragment_habitat() - cut buffer barriers exist assign_patches_to_fragments() + add_patch_area() - label measure connected patches aggregate_connected_patches() - summarise patch areas summarise_connectivity() - compute effective mesh size probability connectedness , equivalently, use habitat_connectivity() data frame output, habitat_connectivity_full() also need intermediate rasters.

title: Using raster vs vector
text: Rasters essentially matrices - grids cells fixed resolution. Vectors essentially polygons - shapes drawn line. See example Luxembourg raster left, colour values correspond elevation. right vector, showing 12 different cantons.  urbioconnect uses rasters work SpatRaster (Spatial Raster) objects. Buffering performed using focal window (terra::focal()), connected patches identified using terra::patches(). vector approach works sf objects. Habitat barriers represented polygons.
